column1: # form<TAB>action<TAB>reason. Reviewed lemma decisions that tools/make-lexicon.py applies after every rule; action: keep (the form is its own lemma) or fold:<lemma> (the form reads as that lemma). Rule: the lemma is the headword a reader sees, translates and saves after tapping the word in a book, so a form is kept when learner's dictionaries give it its own entry (noun, adjective, adverb, preposition or interjection) and that entry is its usual reading (meeting, interested, according, thanks); when the readings are about even, it is kept only if its own headword still fits the other reading while the base word would be taken for another word (meaning, not mean; stuck, not stick). Verb forms, regular plurals and comparatives stay folded (walked, walking, mice, better, lighter, left, lost). A plural follows a kept singular (meetings); it keeps its own headword when its usual meaning is one the singular lacks (glasses, goods, manners) or when the noun is plural-only (scissors, jeans). The generator itself keeps the -ings plural of a folded -ing form (sayings is a noun, never say). Folded here: regular plurals the rules cannot reach, because WordNet lists the plural as a noun of its own (viewers, followers), writes the singular only capitalized (americans, sundays) or lacks the word (smartphones, selfies). fold:<lemma> also corrects a wrong target (lives is mostly the plural of life). Evidence: a teacher's judgement of ordinary reading, checked against part-of-speech counts in UD English-EWT where it has enough (so far all three splits, which is why the lemma evaluation set is also scored without the forms decided here; later reviews use dev and test only); an unclear case keeps the automatic decision. Reviewed: the 400 most frequent flagged folds; among the 30,000 most frequent forms, the classes above; folds into a lemma at least 30 times rarer than the form (outgoing is not outgo).
